To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the tilt/translation ratio should be increased with the level of decelaration and decreased with the level of acceleration.

the tilt/translation ratio should be increased when the deceleration is increased, but the acceleration is generally perceived as overestimated, and this overestimation doesn’t seem to depend on the tilt/translation ratios used.
the best tilt/rotation ratio for the simulation depends on the level (acceleration/deceleration) and on the level of motion (low, medium or high).

the design and evaluation of driving simulation systems for the training of drivers and the evaluation of driver assistance systems.
the development of new motion algorithms for driving simulators that take into account the limitations of human sensory systems and that allow the reproduction of real-world situations.
the development of an algorithm to simulate acceleration and deceleration on dynamic driving simulators.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the tilt/translation ratio should be set at 1 for acceleration, and 0.8 for deceleration.

the simulation of decelaration on a dynamic driving simualtor requires to use the tilt/translation ratio that is the best for the level of decelaraton, whereas the simulation of acceleration can be achieved by using the tilt/translation that is the best at low acceleration level.
for deceleration the simulation of the tilt/translation ratio is important, while for acceleration, the tilt/translation is less important and the level of acceleration is the most important factor.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a tilt/translation ratio of 2/1 for decelerations and of 4/1 for accelerations are the most appropriate for a passive driving simulation on dynamic driving simulator.
the tilt/translation ratio should not be constant, but it should be adapted to the level of motion.
for braking, the best tilt/rotation ratio should be increased when the deceleration level is high.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the simulation of decelaration should be done with tilt/translation ratio depending on the level of acceleration and the simulation of acceleration should be done with a fixed tilt/translation ratio.
a tilt/translation ratio of 2:1 should be applied to simulate deceleration on a dynamic driving simulators.
the simulation of decelaration and acceleration should be considered separately, and that the tilt/translation ratio should not be the same for both situations.
